clues: Rocks normally associated with the deep Earth can be studied here above the surface.
Exposed oceanic crust and mantle material provide evidence for plate tectonics.
Later glaciers added fjords, steep cliffs, valleys and lakes to this geological record.
The protected landscape lies on the western coast of the island of Newfoundland.
Find the Canadian national park famous for its exposed mantle rocks and glacial scenery in western Newfoundland.
targetLabel: Gros Morne National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The park preserves both evidence of plate movement and the effects of later glaciation. Exposed mantle material is a geological exposure, not an opening through which the whole mantle is visible. Its published park point represents the wider protected landscape.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
